summary: Uncommitted LEB128 varint codec (protocol encoding) with a roundtrip test over single-byte values only.

defects.description: The roundtrip test only uses values below 128, so the multi-byte path (continuation bit `| 0x80`, `value >>= 7`, the shift `7 * i`) never runs with more than one byte; mutants there survive. Values such as 128, 300, 16384 and u64::MAX are needed.

Only roundtrips are tested, never the encoded bytes, so a bug made symmetrically in encode and decode (wrong group size, wrong bit order) would pass. This is a wire format, so tests should pin known encodings, e.g. 300 -> [0xAC, 0x02], 1 -> [0x01].
The consumed byte count (`.1` of decode's result) is never asserted, so `i + 1` -> `i * 1` survives. Callers framing a stream depend on it.

`decode_rejects_truncated` asserts only is_err(), not DecodeError::Truncated, and the Overflow path (11+ continuation bytes, `i >= 10`) has no test at all, so `>=` -> `>` and swapping the variants survive.
